prerequisites: Strength of Materials 1: ability to calculate internal forces or sectional forces for statically determinate beam structures
Strength of Materials 1: knowledge of basic concepts of continuum mechanics, especially stress and deformation, and the general problem statement of continuum mechanics

Strength of Materials 1: ability to determine stresses and deformations for simple cross-sections for each type of elementary sectional force (normal force, shear force, bending moment, and torsional moment)

learning_outcomes.text: The student knows the relationship between stresses at a point and can apply simple limit stress hypotheses for ductile (steel, ...) and brittle materials (concrete, soil, ...).

The student is able to determine the deformations and stresses across the cross-section for (a combination of) the four elementary sectional forces (normal force, bending, shear force, torsion) for heterogeneous or composite (steel-concrete composites), massive or thin-walled cross-sections.
The student knows the principle of virtual work and can apply it to calculate displacements in isostatic structures.
The student is able to analyze the buckling of a column or the lateral torsional buckling of a beam.
The student can calculate the stresses in a structure due to impact loading.

syllabus_topics: Mohr's circle, principal stresses at a point
Yield criteria for ductile materials (Tresca-Guest, von Mises)
Fracture criteria for brittle materials (Rankine, Mohr-Coulomb)
(Partial) plastic deformation of cross-sections loaded in bending
Principle of virtual work and Maxwell-Betti reciprocity theorem
Calculation of displacements in structures
Stress distribution in arbitrary cross-sections for elementary sectional forces
Heterogeneous or composite cross-sections (e.g., reinforced concrete)
Skew bending analysis
Stresses in thin-walled cross-sections due to shear and torsion
Elastic instability of structural elements (buckling and lateral torsional buckling)
Analysis of cable structures
Impact loading
The circle of Mohr: relationships between stresses at a point
Limit stress hypotheses for ductile and brittle materials
Plastic deformations: plastic yielding of the cross-section in bending
Composite cross-sections: analysis of stresses and deformations for elementary sectional forces
Calculation of displacements in structures using energy conservation and virtual work
Composite bending - also of materials without tensile strength
Shear and torsion of arbitrary thin-walled cross-sections
Cables
Elastic instability
Impact loading

assessment_methods.method: Written exam during the examination period (open questions, exercises, limited theory questions)

assessment_rules: The exam will consist of assignments (exercises, limited theory questions) to assess the insight into the stress distribution and deformation behavior of beam constructions. Allowed learning materials include a formula sheet and a calculator.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
